title: Advice: find your talent
summary: Thomas urges finding where one's talent lies, citing student Oscar Cohen who went to Joe Glaser's mailroom, and his son the artist.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Right. And I want to go back to something else that's so important.
To find out what your talent is, what you're best in. It's good that you like it, but if you find out what your talent is, proceed in it.
Well, how do you do that, Foots?
Well, you know...it will come to you. It will come to you...
That's not really an answer, "It will come to you."

It will. Now, see, Milt, you must realize that all these things I'm saying is dedicated on the things that happened to me. I can only tell it...give some advice concerning what helped me. Because it was late in life when I found out my talent was in music. I got involved with it and found out I could play different things. See, I had heard so many good musicians, and a talent for music and didn't know it. I went into it and learned about music. But after I learned about it, I found out I could pick up on it easily. It was easy for me. Everything is generally easy for me. It's depending where your talent is. Because I had one guy I taught, and I told him, "Man, you ain't gonna be no saxophone player. You need to go and get into something else." You know who he is? Oscar Cohen. Oscar Cohen was a student of mine at one time.

Yeah. And I could find out that he wasn't diggin' his lessons and hittin' them, and I told him. And he took the advice, and he went to work with Joe Glaser in the mailroom. Of course, Joe Glaser had eyes for what he wanted to do. He wanted him eventually to take over the company. Nobody...

Yeah. Nobody knew it but Joe Glaser. And two or three times, I had guys studying with me, and I found out they wasn't advancing, and I told them, "Forget it. Find something else." On one instrument, I know I proved myself... When I found out that my son had talent for Art, he could draw, I insisted that he went to art school. And he went to art school when he was still going to art school, and he went on to be a good artist.
A great commercial artist. He sure did. Billy(?) Thomas. He did album covers, right?
